questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Two-Variable Function
questions.problem: Evaluate $z=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x-2y+4)$ at the point $(-4,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate our multivariable function at the point $(-4,1),$ we substitute $x=-4$ and $y=1$ into the function expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}z\,{|}_{(-4,1)} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x-2y+4)\,{|}_{(-4,1)} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3(-4)-2(1)+4) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(-12-2+4) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(-10),\end{aligned}
$$

which is undefined.

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Two-Variable Function
questions.problem:
The function $f(x,y)$ is defined as 

$$
f(x,y)=\sqrt[3]{xy+7}.
$$

Evaluate this function at the point $(-4,-5).$
questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate our multivariable function at the point $(-4,-5),$ we substitute $x=-4$ and $y=-5$ into the function expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-4,-5) & =\sqrt[3]{xy+7}\,{|}_{(-4,-5)} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{(-4)(-5)+7} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{20+7} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{27} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Two-Variable Function
questions.problem: Evaluate $z=x\operatorname{ln}⁡y-1$ at the point $(3,{e}^{2}).$
questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate our multivariable function at the point $(3,{e}^{2}),$ we substitute $x=3$ and $y={e}^{2}$ into the function expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}z\,{|}_{(3,{e}^{2})} & =(x\operatorname{ln}⁡y-1){|}_{(3,{e}^{2})} \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})-1 \\  & =3(2\operatorname{ln}⁡e)-1 \\  & =3(2)-1 \\  & =6-1 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The function $f(x,y)$ is defined as 

$$
f(x,y)=x\operatorname{sin}⁡y.
$$

Evaluate this function at the point $(-6,-\frac{\pi }{4}).$
questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate our multivariable function at the point $(-6,-\frac{\pi }{4}),$ we substitute $x=-6$ and $y=-\frac{\pi }{4}$ into the function expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-6,-\frac{\pi }{4}) & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,{|}_{(-6,-\pi /4)} \\  & =-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =-6(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The function $f(x,y)$ is defined as 

$$
f(x,y)=3{y}^{3}-x+2.
$$

Evaluate this function at the point $(5,-1).$
questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate our multivariable function at the point $(5,-1),$ we substitute $x=5$ and $y=-1$ into the function expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(5,-1) & =(3{y}^{3}-x+2){|}_{(5,-1)} \\  & =3(-1)^{3}-5+2 \\  & =-3-5+2 \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: The Domain of a Function Involving Reciprocals and Radicals
questions.problem: Find the domain of the function $f(x,y)=\frac{1}{2x+y}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The function is well-defined at all points $(x,y)$ for which the following condition is satisfied:

- The expression in the denominator is not equal to zero.

As a result, the points in the domain must satisfy the following inequality:

$$
2x+y\ne 0
$$

Therefore, the domain is

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,2x+y\ne 0}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: The Domain of a Function Involving Reciprocals and Radicals
questions.problem: Find the domain of the function $z=\frac{\sqrt{x-1}}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The function is well-defined at all points $(x,y)$ for which the following conditions are satisfied:

- The expression in the denominator is not equal to zero, and

- the expression under the square root is non-negative.

As a result, the points in the domain must satisfy the following inequalities:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-1\ge 0 \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1\ne 0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}x\ge 1 \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\ne 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain is

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,x\ge 1,\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\ne 1}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: The Domain of a Function Containing Exponential, Logarithmic, and Trigonometric Functions
questions.problem: Find the domain of the function $f(x,y)={e}^{{x}^{2}/y}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that

- $\frac{{x}^{2}}{y}$ is defined for $x$ and $y,$ such that $y\ne 0,$ and

- ${e}^{g(x,y)}$ is defined if $g(x,y)$ is defined.

As a result, ${e}^{{x}^{2}/y}$ is defined for values of $x$ and $y$ that satisfy $y\ne 0.$

Therefore, the domain of $f$ is

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y\ne 0}.
$$

questions.problem: Which of the following shaded regions corresponds to the domain of the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The function is well-defined at all points $(x,y)$ for which the following condition is satisfied:

- The expression under the square root is non-negative.

As a result, the points in the domain must satisfy the following inequalities:

$$
{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\ge 0\,⟹\,{y}^{2}\le {x}^{2}\,⟹\,-|x|\le y\le |x|
$$

Therefore, the domain is

$$
D={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-|x|\le y\le |x|}.
$$

Since the inequality involves the $\le $ sign, the curves are part of the domain. Therefore, we draw the solid curves $y=-|x|$ and $y=|x|,$ and shade the area *below* the curve $y=|x|,$ and *above* the curve $y=-|x|.$

The resulting domain is as follows:

$$

Since the expression involves the $>$ sign, the line is *not* part of the domain. Therefore, we draw the dashed line $y=2x$ and shade the region *above* the line.

canonical_examples.problem:
The function $f(x,y)$ is defined as 

$$
f(x,y) = y^2 - \log_3(x - 7).
$$

Evaluate this function at the point $(10,3).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To evaluate our multivariable function at the point $(10,3),$ we substitute $x = 10$ and $y = 3$ into the function expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(10,3) & =({y}^{2}-{log}_{3}⁡(x-7)){|}_{(10,3)} \\  & ={3}^{2}-{log}_{3}⁡(10-7) \\  & =9-{log}_{3}⁡(3) \\  & =9-1 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(10,3)=8.$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the domain of the function $z= \dfrac{\ln (2x+y)}{\sqrt{x}}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The function is well-defined at all points $(x,y)$ for which the following conditions are satisfied:

- the expression in the denominator is not equal to zero, and

$$

$$
\big\{(x, y)\in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, 2x+y >0, \: x > 0 \big\}.
$$
